# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS

# Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) should be performed to rule out infectious

endocarditis. Consult Cardiology or Infectious Diseases for more information.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.

[Approach to Endocarditis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-appro-to-endocarditis)

Follow-up blood cultures should be obtained within 24-48 hours after initiating

antimicrobial therapy.

# Duration of therapy:

Treatment duration requires assessing complexity of infection. Uncomplicated

bacteremia are those who meet the following criteria:

1. Infectious endocarditis has been excluded via TTE

2. Resolution of fever within 3 days of initiating anti-staphylococci

antimicrobial therapy

3. The primary focus of infection has been promptly removed

4. Negative blood cultures within 2-3 days of removing focus of infection and

initiating anti-staphylococci antimicrobial therapy

5. No hematogenous spread of infection to secondary foci

6. No presence of implanted devices

Treat for 2 weeks after last negative blood culture set in uncomplicated

bacteremia. If there is an easily removable or drainable focus (e.g. infected

intravenous catheter, minor abscess, urinary cystitis, or mild to moderate

pneumonia), and this focus has been treated, give parenteral antimicrobials for

2 weeks. Complicated bacteremia requires 4-6 weeks of treatment.

# Treatment of methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) (mec-A

# negative)

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

< OR >

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

# Treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) (mec-A positive)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)
